items.title: Breaking: Australia to provide military support to Gulf states
items.description: Australia will provide military support to Persian Gulf states impacted by Iranian missile and drone attacks.

items.title: Live: Australia grants five Iranian football players asylum
items.description: Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke has confirmed the government has offered humanitarian visas to five Iranian soccer players. Follow live.

items.title: What you need to know about Iran today, with Laura Tingle
items.description: The ABC's global affairs editor, Laura Tingle, is in Dubai and will provide daily updates on the Middle East war.

items.title: Live: Donald Trump says war against Iran is 'very complete'
items.description: Iranian missiles are intercepted over Türkiye, Qatar and United Arab Emirates, as war in the Middle East continues. Follow live.

items.title: 'Every war game': The problem with the US strategy in Iran
items.description: A former top US diplomat says her country's efforts to topple Iran's leadership risks destabilising the region and strengthening the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

items.title: In the early hours of the Iran war, Indonesia's president made a telling offer
items.description: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto's big ambitions on the world stage and at home have alarmed his critics.

items.title: Dubai's 'cringe' influencers have a new rule: Don't mention the war
items.description: As missiles and drones began lighting up the sky over Dubai, many of the city's social media personalities started posting about it. Then the government stepped in.

items.title: Live: ASX 200 set to rebound as Wall Street lifts and oil falls
items.description: After huge losses yesterday spurred by concerns about the economic impact of the Middle East war, the Australian market is set to track Wall Street's overnight rise. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Transport companies at risk of shutting due to rising petrol prices
items.description: Transport companies are at risk of shutting due to the cost of fuel, as global oil prices spike.

items.title: The network of Liberals behind two 'grassroots' childcare campaigns
items.description: The childcare groups say they are the voices for everyday parents. What they don't mention is that they are supported by a network of current and former Liberals.

items.title: Will this year's flu vaccine protect against the fast-moving Super-K strain?
items.description: Experts say they are feeling "nervous" as Australia approached this year's flu season, with a new, fast-moving strain of influenza dubbed "Super-K" circulating as vaccine uptake dwindles.

items.title: Bundaberg region on alert as major flood warning issued
items.description: Thousands of residents are on major flood watch across Queensland following days of huge rainfall totals.

items.title: Thousands of melatonin bottles intercepted at border over safety concerns
items.description: Australian Border Force officials have intercepted more than 150,000 units of melatonin in four months, after authorities warned they would crack down on unregulated products.

items.title: Decline in GP home visits drives vulnerable people into care homes
items.description: The number of GP home visits has declined by 85 per cent in Australia over the past three decades, which doctors say is driving vulnerable people into residential care and hospital prematurely.

items.title: From cattle stations to city streets, how cowboy fashion went mainstream
items.description: From streetwear to festival fits, country fashion has become mainstream in Australian cities and heritage brands are reaping the benefits.

items.title: Maggie Gyllenhaal's Franken-feminist fable fumbles the plot
items.description: The Bride!, a modern retelling of The Bride of Frankenstein, takes massive swings in terms of performances, plotting and subtext, but not all of its gambles pay off.

items.title: ABC Shakespeare quiz: How well doest thou know his characters and quotes?
items.description: A quiz by any other word would smell as sweet, or something, so have a crack at our 10 questions on the works of William Shakespeare.

items.title: Katherine locals survey flood damage as volunteers rally to help
items.description: An "army" of volunteers has hit the streets of Katherine to help residents worst affected by the weekend's flooding, as they survey the damage from near-record river rises.

items.title: Bomb found near Mamdani's home 'act of ISIS-inspired terrorism', police say
items.description: A homemade bomb thrown near an anti-Islam protest in New York at the weekend is being investigated as an Islamic State-inspired act of "terrorism," police say.

items.title: Labor MP says linking Israeli government to antisemitism is 'dangerous'
items.description: Josh Burns also acknowledged the government had not always acted fast enough to deal with antisemitism and said it was necessary to be "humble" in the wake of the Bondi terror attack.

items.title: Matildas learn next opponent as North Korea sensationally protest offside call
items.description: The Matildas will face North Korea in the quarterfinals of the Women's Asian Cup, after the North Koreans go down 2-1 to China in controversial circumstances at a soaking Western Sydney Stadium.

items.title: Lions to contest three-match ban handed to Andrews over swinging arm
items.description: Brisbane begins its season with two pivotal cases at the AFL tribunal in a bid to not have its defensive stocks completely depleted heading into the first month.

items.title: Mardi Gras pioneer wants more inclusive venues in country towns
items.description: After taking part in the original 1978 Mardi Gras parade, Kevin Betts returned to his country roots and set about making life easier for people growing up queer in the regions.

items.title: Forwarded email a rare public glimpse into the cunning world of political spin
items.description: It is common for media advisors to provide reporters with background information in an effort to shape the way a story is reported, but the practice backfired spectacularly when the SA government shared an email from the wrong patient.

items.title: Scientists warn axing CSIRO jobs will harm climate change response
items.description: Scientists are calling on the Australian government to push back on a plan to scrap hundreds of jobs at the nation's science agency, as they await the release of further details this week.
